title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche-era birational anabelian programme). K is a field of finite type over Q, k is the algebraic closure of Q in K, and Γ = Gal(Q̄/k). π_K = Gal(K̄/K·Q̄) is the 'geometric' Galois group of the function field. E_K = Gal(K̄/K) fits into 1 → π_K → E_K → Γ → 1. B_K is the étale topos of Spec K, i.e. the classifying topos of E_K.

The page continues the previous one. There Grothendieck proposed that Γ-equivariant outer homomorphisms π_{K'} → π_K with open image should come only from field embeddings K ⊂ K'.

1. Why the open-image or non-degeneracy hypothesis is indispensable. Take K' = k, so π_{K'} = 1. The trivial homomorphism is Γ-equivariant, and without such a hypothesis one would 'find a homomorphism K → k', which is absurd since K is transcendental.

2. A finer condition. Work with homomorphisms π_{K'} → π_K instead of E_{K'} → E_K, and require that the centralizer in π_K of the image of every open subgroup of π_{K'} be trivial. Grothendieck calls such a homomorphism 'admissible'.

3. What admissibility buys. With trivial centralizers, a Γ-commuting outer homomorphism lifts uniquely to a morphism of extensions E_{K'} → E_K over Γ. This is the standard fact that, when centralizers are trivial, outer data determine the extension map. That morphism of extensions is 'the truly essential object'.

4. The degenerate case recast. For K' = k one has E_{K'} = Γ. The interesting objects are then not the Γ-homomorphisms (1) → π_K but the sections of E_K → Γ: the birational section-conjecture situation.

5. Question-conjecture (continued on the next page). For K, K' finitely generated over Q and a morphism of topoi B_{K'} → B_K over B_Q (equivalently a Γ_Q-compatible outer homomorphism E_{K'} → E_K), the following should be equivalent:
- (a) it comes from a field embedding K ⊂ K';
- (b) it has open image;
- (c) it is admissible.
The next page already notes that (c) is too weak.

This is the Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture for finitely generated fields, together with a first look at the birational section conjecture.
errors: No outright error on this page. The 'admissible' condition (trivial centralizers of images of open subgroups) is offered as the minimal working hypothesis. On the next page Grothendieck himself notes that it is not strong enough to force geometricity. Open image (condition b) is the hypothesis eventually used in the literature.

The formulation via π_{K'} → π_K 'instead of E_{K'} → E_K' is only heuristically justified. Unique lifting needs triviality of centralizers in π_K. Existence of the lift needs the outer homomorphism to be compatible with the given outer Γ-actions, which is implicitly assumed in 'commutant à Γ'.

ideas.what: Γ-equivariant outer homomorphisms of geometric Galois groups of function fields should come from field embeddings, provided a non-degeneracy (open image) condition holds; the K'=k example shows the condition is necessary
ideas.modern_name: Hom-form of the birational anabelian (Neukirch–Uchida–Pop type) conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture); Pop 1994 (isomorphism form for finitely generated fields); Mochizuki (Hom-form results over sub-p-adic fields); extent of the full Hom-form for finitely generated fields: unsure
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated); letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (anabelian section)

ideas.what: 'Admissible' homomorphism: the centralizer in π_K of the image of every open subgroup of π_{K'} is trivial, so that outer Γ-homomorphisms lift uniquely to morphisms of extensions
ideas.modern_name: Centre-freeness / trivial-centralizer ('slimness') condition used to pass between outer homomorphisms and morphisms of extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; the term 'slim' is Mochizuki's
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche itself; unsure

ideas.what: In the degenerate case K'=k, the relevant objects are the sections of E_K → Γ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1983 letter to Faltings); results by Koenigsmann, Pop, Esnault–Wittenberg and others
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (section conjecture); La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Formulating the conjecture as morphisms of classifying topoi B_{K'} → B_K over B_Q
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian conjecture phrased via étale (classifying) topoi
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (topos-theoretic formulation); La Longue Marche

missed.claim: Explicit draft stage in which a trivial-centralizer ('admissible') condition is proposed as a possible substitute for open image in the Hom-form birational conjecture, and then judged insufficient on the next page. This shows how Grothendieck converged on the open-image hypothesis that later became standard. It is historical detail, not new mathematics.
missed.quote: supposer que le centralisateur dans π_K de l'image de tout groupe ouvert de π_{K'} soit réduit à (1) – on dira que l'homomorphisme en question est admissible
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for the genesis of the hypotheses in Pop's and Mochizuki's Hom-form theorems. The mathematical content is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are the familiar Longue Marche / Faltings-letter anabelian conjectures (birational Hom-form, section conjecture). The only unpublished detail is the short-lived 'admissible' (trivial centralizer) condition, which Grothendieck himself discards.
